extracted.intended_audience: poets, poetic critics, and aspiring writers (Coleridge and literary friends in particular)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing, revising, and judging poetry (sonnets, odes, blank verse, epic), given as letters of critique and advice to a contemporary poet. Emphasizes tone, proportion, diction, originality, and fitness of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain proportionality of texture and incident
rubrics_metrics.description: The texture will be most lamentably disproportionate if lofty subject-matter is annexed to low, cock-and-a-bull incidents (e.g., degrading the Joan of Arc into a pot-girl with ale-house episodes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mixing the sublime with trivial or domestic detail in a way that jars; if you introduce low incidents into a sublime poem, ensure they are harmonized in tone and purpose rather than creating disproportion. Anti-pattern: a majestic prelude followed by a homely, incongruous scene that undercuts the mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve character-integrity and historical tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not transmogrify the subject (e.g., turning a sainted fanatic into a modern novel-ish proselyte); preserve the proper character and historical dignity of figures like Joan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid anachronistic modernizations or trivializations that make a historical/heroic figure read as a contemporary caricature. Check for consistency in characterization across the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and muscularity of lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the 'utter want of all rhythm, the monotony and dead plumb-down of the pauses, and the absence of all bone, muscle, and sinew in the single lines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rhythmic variety and dynamic cadences; lines should have strength ('bone, muscle, and sinew') and avoid flat, monotonous pauses. Revise lines that read plodding or lifeless. Example anti-pattern: long, undifferentiated blank-verse lines that produce no musical or rhetorical lift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality—avoid close imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not produce a 'faint copy' of another poet's distinctive phrase or tone (e.g., 'fierce vivacity' as a pale copy of another's 'fierce and terrible benevolence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for original turns of phrase and images; if readers will naturally compare you to a living contemporary, steer sufficiently away in diction or approach to avoid unfavorable rivalry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity in delineating common feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: In delineations of common and natural feelings, aim for simplicity rather than affected ornament; avoid sad deviations from simplicity when that is the aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain, direct expression for familiar emotions; resist over-elaboration or ornate phrasing that obscures feeling. Anti-pattern: florid or overworked language for quotidian emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of imagery—avoid confused metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not confuse ideas in a single image (e.g., 'The hot, sore brain attributes its own hues of ghastliness and torture' as a shocking confusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep metaphors coherent and logically consistent; revise images that mix incompatible senses or actions. If an image reads as muddled, simplify or reframe it to a single, clear comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose specifics plausibly and avoid ludicrous phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick concrete particulars that are plausible and avoid details that read ludicrously (e.g., 'canvas-coverture moving' or oddly counted specifics like 'a woman and six children' that invite unintended questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting concrete details, consider how plausible and affecting they will seem to readers; change specifics that distract or produce unintended comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish the interior emotional portrait of prophets/fanatics
rubrics_metrics.description: In accounts of a fanatic or a prophet, the description of their emotions is expected to be most highly finished and is central to the piece's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus attention (and rhetorical resources) on interior states when depicting inspired figures; allow the emotions to be richly and precisely rendered rather than relying solely on external action or didactic commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match versification to thought and measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Versification should be 'fitted to the thoughts'—the measure and rhythm must suit the subject and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure meter, line-length, and prosodic choices support the poem's content. Rework awkward metrical passages to better reflect the intended tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contrivance—no 'made-dishes at the muses' banquet'
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject artificial, contrived phrases and poetical devices that feel cooked-up rather than arising naturally from feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor organic expression; excise contrived epithets, forced conceits, and ornament that doesn't serve the thought. Anti-pattern: lines that call attention to cleverness rather than depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select diction consistent with connotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose words whose connotations fit the kind of inspiration or mood (e.g., 'turbid ecstasy' suggests muddy inspiration unsuited to lofty prophetic inspiration—'troublous' may be preferable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review key adjectives and modifiers for associative fit; replace terms that carry inappropriate imagery or register for the context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heighten emotional impact—avoid lines that diminish it
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer lines that intensify a scene's terror or pathos and avoid phrases that take away their force (e.g., 'hailed him immortal' which diminishes the terror of death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing, ask whether each line increases the intended effect; remove or rework lines that blur or lessen emotional stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concrete particulars over vague generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid too-general summaries ('his eventful years all come and gone') and favor concrete particulars (make him a soldier or another specific character to lend realism and interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify occupational or biographical details to deepen narrative credibility and emotional investment. If a generality feels slack, supply a telling specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for appropriately ambitious form when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a poet has the capacity, attempt a larger, more ample form (e.g., an epic) rather than restricting oneself to occasional odes or sonnets; 'having one great end to direct all your poetical faculties' can realize genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match ambition of subject and talent to the scale of the work; consider sustained, large-scale projects to develop and display full poetic powers rather than only minor occasional pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication choices: prioritize self-approval, then peer consensus; attend to presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: First a man should be pleased with his own work, then seek approval among friends (taste may safely be put to the vote); print sonnets 'verbatim' as intended and make careful decisions about inclusions and copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a volume, preserve the author's intended wording; be selective about what to include—omit parts that lack originality or coherence. Practical note: send only a small number of complimentary copies (three to six).
